newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tunisia's CPI up 0.6 percent in Jan-Feb.
newsitem.headline: Tunisia's CPI up 0.6 percent in Jan-Feb.

text.p: Tunisia's consumer price index (CPI) rose by 0.6 percent in January-February 1997 compared to its level in December 1996, a Tunisian senior official said on Tuesday.

The average level of consumer prices during the first two months of the year is put at 3.4 percent compared to 5.2 percent during the corresponding period of 1996, Economic Development Minister Taoufik Baccar told journalists at a briefing.
"These figures show that we continue to control the consumer prices, but one must continue to be vigilant," Baccar commented.
Inflation as measured by the CPI was 3.7 percent for the whole year 1996 from 6.3 percent in 1995.
The cut in the inflation rate for 1996 was made possible by the decrease of prices of foodstuffs thanks to rainfall which led to higher agriculture output after a two-year drought.
CPI is forecast to rise by 4.2 percent in 1997.
